subject: english
question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The victim was ______ in the back of his head.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Shot**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**shot**" is the correct choice to fill in the blank in the sentence.
 
• "shot" - This is the past participle form of the verb "shoot."
 
• In this context, it is used to describe an action that has already happened, indicating that the victim was indeed shot in the back of his head.
 
• When describing actions that occurred in the past, it's common to use the past participle form of the verb, which is "shot."
 
• So, the most appropriate option is "**shot**" because it correctly conveys the past action of someone being shot in the back of their head.

Hence, **option 1** is the correct answer.

**Complete sentence**: *The victim was shot __in the back of his head.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "**Shooting**" is the present participle form of the verb "shoot." It indicates an ongoing action, which is not suitable for this sentence because it describes a completed action.
 
• "**Shoot**" is the base form of the verb and does not fit in this context as it doesn't convey the past tense required for the sentence.
 
• "**Shooted**" is not a correct word in standard English. The past tense of "shoot" is "shot," not "shooted."
